paragraphs: There are two different ways to create a thread in Java. We have listed them as follows:

• By Implementing a Runnable Interface
• By Extending a Thread Class

sections.heading: Create a Thread by Implementing a Runnable Interface
paragraphs: If your class is intended to be executed as a thread then you can achieve this by implementing a Runnable interface. You will need to follow three basic steps −

sections.heading: Example to Create a Thread by Implementing a Runnable Interface
paragraphs: In this example, we're creating a class RunnableDemo by implementing Runnable interface. RunnableDemo class has run() method implementation. In main class TestThread, we've created the RunnableDemo objects and using those objects we've created two Thread objects. When Thread.start() method is called on each thread objects, threads start processing and program is executed.

sections.heading: Create a Thread by Extending a Thread Class
paragraphs: The second way to create a thread is to create a new class that extends Thread class using the following two simple steps. This approach provides more flexibility in handling multiple threads created using available methods in Thread class.

sections.heading: Example: Demonstrating sleep() Method
paragraphs: In this example, we're showcasing use of sleep() method to delay the processing. It helps in showing the parallel processing in the output. We've added Thread.sleep() call in the run method. InterruptedException is handled as thread can be interrupted during sleep mode.
